description: A three-panel set of secondary-electron SEM micrographs of the near-fracture regions of a Fe-20Mn-6Al-0.6C-0.15Si austenitic low-density steel after Charpy impact testing at three temperatures: (a) −196 °C, (b) −77 °C and (c) room temperature (RT). All three panels carry a 20 µm scale bar in the bottom-right corner and show the same grey ductile matrix cut by dark fracture/void regions along the upper-left edges. Yellow arrows mark the planar-glide features (closely spaced straight slip-band traces / river-like parallel lineations). In (a) only two arrows are drawn and the planar-glide traces are sparse and confined to small localised regions. In (b) three arrows mark more numerous and more clearly developed parallel slip traces. In (c) six arrows mark the most abundant and most pronounced planar-glide bands, which sweep across most of the field of view, together with a large dark elongated void/flaw in the centre-left. The number and prominence of arrowed planar-glide features increase monotonically from −196 °C to RT, so the figure demonstrates visually that planar glide becomes progressively more pronounced as the impact-test temperature rises, and that only a few regions experienced planar glide at −196 °C.

subfigures.description: SEM micrograph near the fracture of the specimen impact-tested at −196 °C, with a 20 µm scale bar. A large white/black fracture-and-void region occupies the upper-left; the matrix shows only sparse, locally confined planar-glide/slip-band traces, marked by two yellow arrows.

SEM micrograph near the fracture of the specimen impact-tested at −77 °C, with a 20 µm scale bar. Dark fracture region along the upper-left edge; planar-glide slip-band traces are more numerous and better developed than in (a), marked by three yellow arrows.

SEM micrograph near the fracture of the specimen impact-tested at room temperature (RT), with a 20 µm scale bar. Dark fracture region at the upper-left and a dark elongated void in the centre-left; planar-glide slip-band traces are the most abundant and pronounced of the three panels, marked by six yellow arrows.

observations.observation: Three SEM micrographs are shown side by side, each labelled with a 20 µm scale bar in the bottom-right corner.
Panel (a) corresponds to the impact test at −196 °C, (b) to −77 °C and (c) to room temperature (RT), as printed in the caption.
Yellow arrows mark planar-glide features: two arrows in (a), three in (b) and six in (c), so the number of marked planar-glide regions increases with increasing test temperature.
Only few regions show planar-glide features in panel (a), the −196 °C impact specimen.
The citing text states that planar glide becomes more pronounced as the deformation temperature increases.
All three panels show a grey ductile matrix adjacent to dark fracture/void regions along the upper-left edge of the field of view.
The planar-glide features appear as closely spaced, roughly parallel straight slip-band traces (river-like lineations) crossing dimpled/smooth matrix areas.
Panel (c) additionally contains a large dark elongated void/flaw in the centre-left of the field of view.

The citing text argues that these planar-glide features could retard crack propagation and thus increase toughness, so the weaker planar glide at lower temperature explains the weaker resistance to crack propagation.
The micrographs are secondary-electron images of near-fracture regions after Charpy impact testing; no magnification value or accelerating voltage is printed on the panels.

unreadable_items: No magnification or accelerating voltage is printed on any panel; only the 20 µm scale bar is legible.
